thread:
omar: Quick Q — saw a spike in 502/504s on prod around 10:05 UTC. Where's the canonical place to look (dashboards / traces / logs) to correlate timeouts vs backend overload? Also want to propose tuning the alert; current pager went off twice last week for what looked like a short blip.

lucy: Start with the "HTTP Error Rates" Grafana panel (prod cluster). Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/http-errors-prod (bookmark). It has per-service 4xx/5xx, and a top-10 routes table. For traces use Honeycomb: https://ui.honeycomb.io/redwood/datasets/prod-traces/query — filter by trace.status or http.status_code.

devon: For logs, Kibana query that helped me: `http.response.status: (502 OR 504) AND @timestamp:[now-30m TO now] AND env:prod` — then group by upstream_host or upstream_service. Often 504s map to slow upstreams (model servers) or LB timeouts.

lucy: Also check the ingress (nginx) error log in the cluster: `kubectl -n ingress logs deploy/nginx-ingress -c controller --since=15m` — if you see `upstream timed out` lines that's an LB->upstream timeout.

omar: thanks — do you have a suggested Alertmanager/prometheus rule we can use? current alert is firing on `increase(nginx_5xx[5m]) > 0` which is... noisy.

devon: Proposed PromQL to replace it (less noisy, groups by route and accounts for request volume):
```
sum by (route, service) (rate(http_requests_total{job="gateway",status=~"5.."}[5m]))
/
sum by (route, service) (rate(http_requests_total{job="gateway"}[5m]))
```
Trigger when this error-rate > 0.02 (2%) and absolute 5xx rate > 0.5 req/s for 5m. That avoids firing on tiny routes.

lucy: +1. Also add a suppression for maintenance windows and a cooldown: `for: 10m` so short blips don't page. For 504-specific investigation, add a tag `error_type: timeout` in the runbook so oncall knows to check model worker queues and pod CPU.

sre-oncall: Adding runbook note: If alert triggers with high 504 fraction: 1) Check Grafana panel (ingress vs service) 2) Check pods for OOM/CPU throttling: `kubectl top pods -n prod` 3) Check model-serving queues (rabbitmq/redis) 4) If ingestion rates are normal but latency high, scale dedicated inference pool or failover to canary model variant.

infra-bot: alert-manager:change deployed for rule `gateway_error_rate_high` -> conditions: error_rate>0.02 AND errors>0.5, for:10m. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412 :thumbsup:

omar: Awesome — I'll open a small PR to update the alert text + add the runbook link. Any objections to starting at 2% threshold? we can lower if it misses issues.

devon: 2% is safe for gateway-level. For edge routes with low volume maybe 5% threshold or add per-route overrides.

lucy: One more tip — when correlating traces, filter by `peer.service` to quickly see if it's an upstream model server vs gateway. That saved me yesterday.

omar: Great, thanks everyone. I'll post the PR and tag @sre-oncall for review.

sre-oncall: Thanks — will review once PR is up. If we see repeat flaps after change, we'll revert to the previous sensitivity and run a short postmortem.
